```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 96
)
```

**The brief:** the preseason guide wants a map of college football: every FBS
program as its logo, sitting on its home stadium, so a reader can find the
schools near them, click one for its stadium and capacity, and show one
conference at a time. This recipe is new, not the interactive version of a
static one. The stadiums come from CollegeFootballData.com through cfbfastR,
leaflet draws the map, and sdvplotR's `addSdvLogoMarkers()` turns each marker
into a team logo.

CollegeFootballData.com needs a free API key in `CFBD_API_KEY` (get one at
<https://collegefootballdata.com/key>; see `?cfbfastR::register_cfbd`). Without
one, the code below is shown but not run.

```{r cfbd-key}
has_key <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("CFBD_API_KEY"))
if (!has_key) cat("CFBD_API_KEY is not set, so the chunks below are shown but not run.\n")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_key)
```

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(leaflet)
library(ggplot2)

season <- 2025
```

## 1. Get the data

`cfbd_team_info()` returns one row per school, and with `only_fbs = TRUE` and a
`year` it is that season's FBS teams with their conference and home venue:
stadium name, city, state, latitude, longitude and capacity. No join is needed.
CFBD's `team_id` is ESPN's team id, the id sdvplotR keys college teams by, so it
goes to the logo functions as it is. That skips name matching, where
`"Charlotte"` alone could be the 49ers or the Saints.

```{r data}
stadiums <- cfbfastR::cfbd_team_info(only_fbs = TRUE, year = season) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  transmute(
    team = as.character(team_id), school, conference,
    venue = venue_name, city, state, capacity,
    lon = longitude, lat = latitude
  ) |>
  arrange(conference, school)
nrow(stadiums)
count(stadiums, conference)
```

A popup is HTML, so the text that goes into it is escaped first (`Texas A&M`
has an ampersand):

```{r popups}
esc <- htmltools::htmlEscape
stadiums <- stadiums |>
  mutate(popup = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b><br>%s<br>%s<br>Capacity %s<br>%s, %s",
    esc(school), esc(conference), esc(venue), format(capacity, big.mark = ","), esc(city), state
  ))
```

## 2. The map

Start with the logos. `addSdvLogoMarkers()` reads the coordinates and team ids
from the map's data with formulas, and `label` is the text shown on hover. A
light basemap keeps the logos readable, and `fitBounds()` frames the
continental United States (Hawai'i is off the frame; zoom out to find it).

```{r map-logos}
lower48 <- c(-125, 24, -66.5, 49.5) # west, south, east, north

leaflet(stadiums) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addSdvLogoMarkers(~lon, ~lat, ~team, league = "cfb", size = 26, label = ~school) |>
  fitBounds(lower48[1], lower48[2], lower48[3], lower48[4])
```

Hover names the school. Add the popup, and a click opens the stadium details:

```{r map-popups}
leaflet(stadiums) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addSdvLogoMarkers(~lon, ~lat, ~team, league = "cfb", size = 26, label = ~school, popup = ~popup) |>
  fitBounds(lower48[1], lower48[2], lower48[3], lower48[4])
```

The Southeast is crowded at this zoom. Put each conference's markers in its own
leaflet group, and `addLayersControl()` lists the groups with a checkbox each,
so the reader can show one conference, or compare two:

```{r map-conferences}
stadium_map <- leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron)
for (conf in unique(stadiums$conference)) {
  stadium_map <- stadium_map |>
    addSdvLogoMarkers(
      ~lon, ~lat, ~team,
      league = "cfb", size = 26, label = ~school, popup = ~popup, group = conf,
      data = filter(stadiums, conference == conf)
    )
}
stadium_map <- stadium_map |>
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = unique(stadiums$conference),
    options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)
  ) |>
  fitBounds(lower48[1], lower48[2], lower48[3], lower48[4])
stadium_map
```

The map has no data of its own here, so each call passes its conference's rows
with `data =`, and the formulas read those.

## 3. Share it

`htmlwidgets::saveWidget()` writes the map to one HTML file;
`selfcontained = TRUE` inlines leaflet's JavaScript, so the file opens anywhere.
The logos and map tiles stay links, so the file needs the network when it is
opened.

```{r save-html}
html <- tempfile("cfb-stadiums-", fileext = ".html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(stadium_map, html, selfcontained = TRUE, title = "FBS stadiums")
round(file.size(html) / 1024) # kilobytes
```

## 4. The static version

For a print page or a post, draw the same logos with ggplot2 at their longitude
and latitude over the state outlines from `map_data("state")` (it needs the
maps package). `coord_quickmap()` keeps the map's proportions. Hawai'i is left
out to keep the frame on the lower 48.

```{r export, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.2, fig.alt = "Map of the lower 48 United States with state outlines and the logo of every FBS college football program in 2025 at its home stadium, dense in the Southeast and Midwest."}
states <- map_data("state")
mainland <- filter(stadiums, state != "HI")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(
    data = states, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "grey97", colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_sdv_logos(data = mainland, aes(x = lon, y = lat, team = team), league = "cfb", height = 0.04) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(
    title = paste("Every FBS program at its home stadium,", season),
    caption = "Data: CollegeFootballData.com via cfbfastR | Viz: sdvplotR"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
